title: AI Dev 26 x SF: Andrew Ng: The Future of Software Engineering
summary: Andrew Ng at AI Dev 26: near-100% AI-written code, product management as the new bottleneck, small generalist teams, Context Hub and Code Dream.

assertions.quote: if I got to review the code, then I become the bottleneck, and it also doesn't work

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
The paper recommends careful review of AI code whatever the tool, along with static analysis, tests, security checks, and monitoring after merge.

assertions.quote: getting only 80% of the way there feels very different

verdicts.note: Removing the last human-written fraction removes a serial bottleneck for some teams, but it relies on reduced review; no controlled evidence, and risk rises for critical code.

assertions.quote: deciding what to build or the product management work becomes the new bottleneck

verdicts.note: Consistent with Amdahl-style reasoning and reports of shifting PM:engineer ratios; evidence is mostly anecdotal from AI-native teams.

assertions.quote: very small teams, they're all kind of generalists

verdicts.note: Some companies report smaller teams and AI-native startups run lean, but industry-wide team-size data are thin and confounded by cost cutting.

assertions.quote: engineers who shape products or product managers that can code can move really fast

verdicts.note: The trend toward 'product engineers' and DevOps ownership predates AI; AI plausibly speeds it, but evidence is anecdotal.

assertions.quote: the job apocalypse is not being nearly as bad as people are hyping it up to be

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: if you ask Claude Code to call the OpenAI API, it will use the chat completions API, which is older and deprecated

verdicts.note: Training cutoffs reliably cause stale version and model suggestions; checking against current docs is necessary.
